text:
ashley: customer reports intermittent 401 followed by 429s when calling /v1/generate. started after they upgraded to sdk-js@2.4.1. example request-id from last failure: req_20260317_abc123xyz. they see 401 ~1/10 requests, then 429 on retries. attached top-level logs show `Invalid API key` then `rate limit exceeded`.
sam: can you capture a minimal curl and tiny SDK repro? also want exact timestamps and the request-ids for each failure. please include sdk versions and region. thanks.
ashley: short curl that reproduces it for us (no real key):
```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"hello"}'
```
ashley: Python minimal (requests) — runs in a loop to hit the problem quickly:
```python
import requests
import time

url = "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer REDACTED_KEY",
           "Content-Type": "application/json",
           "User-Agent": "customer-app/1.2.3"}

for i in range(30):
    r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"ping"})
    print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
```
ashley: Node (fetch) tiny repro as requested:
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  for (let i=0;i<30;i++){
    const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED_KEY',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'User-Agent': 'customer-node/0.1'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-alpha-1', input: 'ping' })
    });
    console.log(i, res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'));
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 400));
  }
})();
```
ashley: Go example (net/http):
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "io/ioutil"
)
func main(){
  client := &http.Client{}
  for i:=0;i<30;i++{
    req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer([]byte(`{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"ping"}`)))
    req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer REDACTED_KEY")
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
    resp, err := client.Do(req)
    if err!=nil { fmt.Println(i, "err", err); continue }
    id := resp.Header.Get("x-request-id")
    body, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    resp.Body.Close()
    fmt.Println(i, resp.StatusCode, id, string(body)[:80])
  }
}
```
eli: a few quick asks for the debug bundle so SRE can triage:
- please attach request-ids for every failure (x-request-id header)
- timestamps (UTC) for each failing call
- SDK version + exact language runtime (node/python/go) and any proxies
- HAR/pcap if they go through a proxy or Cloudflare-like front
- full server response headers and body for 401/429
- set REDWOOD_DEBUG=client to capture client-side SDK traces
sam: thanks — also include rate-limit headers (x-rw-rate-limit, x-rw-remaining, x-rw-reset) if present. if they repro locally, ask them to run the loop above and paste the first 10 lines output.


support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-314 created and linked to thread (priority: high) — assigned to sre-oncall.
sre-oncall: initial theory: intermittent auth failures could be caused by their CI rotating keys or a proxy stripping Authorization header leading to downstream 401 then client backoff triggers 429 on concurrencies. next steps:
- ask customer to run single-request curl with verbose to confirm Authorization header reaches our edge: `curl -v` shows request headers.
- ask for upstream proxy logs if present.
- tell them to paste the exact `x-request-id` lines from the scripts above.
ashley: customer ran `curl -v` and confirmed Authorization is present at their edge, but they have an internal token agent that occasionally returns a 401 and retries with a stale token — attaching agent logs now.
sam: good. once we have their agent logs + request-ids I'll grep our logs for those ids and check edge vs origin behavior. if we see header present at edge but missing at origin, it's an internal proxy issue; if present all the way, we need to inspect our auth service trace.
eli: FYI - if you want a quick temporary mitigation tell them to use a short client-side delay and jitter on retries (exponential backoff) and surface any 401s instead of auto-retrying 1:1, that avoids hitting rate limits during token churn.
ashley: attaching HAR and agent logs, plus output of the python loop — first 12 lines showing mixed 401/429/200 with request ids.
sam: 👍 created a search for those ids in our logging cluster. leaving notes here, will update when I have the origin-side header traces.
support-bot: update: logs found for req_20260317_abc123xyz, traced through edge->auth->origin, auth responded 401 with reason "token not found" then an immediate retry from client produced a 429 due to short retry bursts. escalation ticket updated.
sre-oncall: next step: provide them a short checklist to improve repro fidelity and ask them to attach a debug bundle tar.gz with:
  - agent logs (timestamps)
  - har/console export
  - output of minimal SDK loops (first 20 lines)
  - sdk version + uname

ashley: pinging customer for bundle. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
